page: Amazon Web Services c8i-flex.8xlarge is a compute-optimized cloud instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor and powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor operating at 3.9 GHz. The system provides 16 physical cores and 32 vCPUs, backed by a 480 MB L3 cache alongside hardware support for AVX-512 and Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX). Memory capacity totals 64 GB of DDR5 RAM running at 7 GHz, delivering 2.0 GB of memory per vCPU. The instance does not include integrated local NVMe storage or discrete GPUs, and provides an 8 Gbps baseline network bandwidth.

Performance benchmarks show strong performance in CPU-intensive operations, file processing, and text execution. Synthetic testing achieved strong Geekbench multi-core performance at 17,709 points and single-threaded gzip compression speeds of 33.95 GB/sec. Small language model inference reached 377.41 tokens per second for text generation using a 135M model. Large block memory read bandwidth measured 167.46 GB/sec while write bandwidth recorded 75.85 GB/sec.

Because the instance features a burstable CPU allocation model, it provides resource efficiency for workloads with fluctuating utilization profiles. The absence of local disk drives requires external block storage attachment, presenting an I/O tradeoff for storage-centric applications. The instance is well suited for text analytics, batch processing pipelines, static web serving, and small-scale machine learning inference.
description: Amazon Web Services c8i-flex.8xlarge is a compute-optimized, burstable instance powered by a 3.9 GHz Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor with 16 physical cores and 32 vCPUs on the Nitro hypervisor. It is equipped with 64 GB of 7 GHz DDR5 memory, a 480 MB L3 cache, and hardware extensions including AVX-512 and AMX. The instance lacks local NVMe storage and dedicated GPUs, relying on an 8 Gbps baseline network interface. Benchmark results highlight strong performance in text processing, file compression, and small-model LLM text generation, while memory bandwidth and Redis throughput remain in average benchmark tiers. The burstable CPU model delivers flexibility for variable compute demands, making the instance well suited for batch compute jobs, web serving, text analytics, and small-scale model inference.
